title: The Wizard of Oz · 3. The Tin Woodman and the Lion
source: Retold from L. Frank Baum, The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900), public domain. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/55

text: The road led into a deep, dark forest.
Suddenly they heard a groan from among the trees.
pages.alt: The road leads into a dark forest

text: A man made entirely of tin stood very still with his axe raised high.
"Please oil my joints," he groaned. "I have rusted, and I cannot move."
pages.alt: A rusted Tin Woodman stands frozen with his axe raised

text: Dorothy found an oil can in his cottage. She oiled his neck, his arms, and his legs.
Slowly the Tin Woodman lowered his axe and smiled.
"I have no heart," said the Tin Woodman sadly. "May I come and ask the Wizard for one?"
pages.alt: The Tin Woodman wishes for a heart

text: Just then a terrible roar rang through the forest, and a great Lion sprang onto the road.
He knocked the Scarecrow over and opened his mouth wide at Toto.
Dorothy rushed forward and slapped the Lion on the nose.
"Don't you dare bite Toto! You should be ashamed of yourself, a big beast like you!"
pages.alt: Dorothy slaps the Lion on the nose

text: "I know," said the Lion, wiping a tear with his paw. "I am a coward."
"I roar so others will be afraid of me, but inside I am scared of everything."
pages.alt: The Lion admits he is a coward

text: "Perhaps the Wizard will give me courage," said the Lion.
So the four friends and Toto walked on together toward the Emerald City.
pages.alt: Four friends walk toward the Emerald City

questions.ask: What did the Tin Woodman need so he could move?
What did the Tin Woodman wish for?
Who said he was a coward?
